title: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (Modular) · Unit 2 (4WM2H/01) — original full-length mock
subject: pearson-igcse-mathematics-a-modular
subjectLabel: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (Modular)
instructions: Answer all 22 questions. The total time is 2 hours; there is no separate reading period. Write your answer and all working in each question's response area; add pages if needed. A permitted scientific calculator may be used. The Formula reference attached to every question contains the tier-specific supplied formula facts. Draw your own labelled diagrams or graphs where requested; all necessary coordinates and measurements are provided. Do not infer measurements from a sketch. Use a suitable scale and label axes. Give units where appropriate. Keep unrounded working; give non-exact final numerical answers to 3 significant figures unless otherwise stated. This is an original DigitalDP practice paper, not a Pearson paper. Digital drawing is a classroom adaptation, not a test of physical ruler-and-compass accuracy.

resources.label: Higher formula reference
resources.text:
Formula reference — independently typeset mathematical facts
Trapezium: area = ½(a + b)h, where a and b are parallel side lengths and h is perpendicular height.
Prism: volume = cross-sectional area × length.
Cylinder: volume = πr²h; curved surface area = 2πrh. Here r is radius and h is perpendicular height.
Arithmetic series: Sₙ = n[2a + (n − 1)d]/2, where a is the first term and d is the common difference.
Quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0 (a ≠ 0): x = [−b ± √(b² − 4ac)]/(2a).
Triangle ABC: sides a, b, c lie opposite angles A, B, C respectively.
Sine rule: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C.
Cosine rule: a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A.
Triangle area = ½ab sin C.
Right circular cone: volume = πr²h/3; curved surface area = πrl, where l is slant height.
Sphere: volume = 4πr³/3; surface area = 4πr².

questions.label: Question 1 — Discount and original price
questions.prompt: A tablet sells for $276 after a reduction of 8%. (a) Find the original price. [3] (b) A shop buys one at $240 and sells it for $276. Find the percentage profit on the buying price. [2]

questions.label: Question 2 — Simultaneous equations
questions.prompt: (a) Solve 4x + 3y = 29 and 2x − y = 7. [4] (b) Find 3x − 2y using your solution. [1]

questions.label: Question 3 — Arithmetic sequence
questions.prompt: An arithmetic sequence begins 11, 17, 23, 29. (a) Find the nth term. [2] (b) Find the 30th term. [1] (c) Show that 202 is not a term. [2]

questions.label: Question 4 — Changing the subject
questions.prompt: (a) Make x the subject of y = 5x − 7. [2] (b) Make h the subject of A = ½(a + b)h. [2] (c) Use your formula to find h when A = 54, a = 7 and b = 11. [1]

questions.label: Question 5 — Standard form in context
questions.prompt: A file contains 3.2 × 10⁸ bytes. (a) Write this as an ordinary number. [1] (b) A device stores 7.5 × 10¹¹ bytes. Find the greatest whole number of these files that it can store. [3] (c) Write the total size of 25 files in standard form. [1]

questions.label: Question 6 — Triangular prism
questions.prompt: A right prism has a right-triangle cross-section with perpendicular sides 6 cm and 8 cm. The prism is 15 cm long. (a) Find its volume. [2] (b) Find its total surface area. [3]

questions.label: Question 7 — Transformation and similarity
questions.prompt: Triangle A has vertices (1,2), (3,2), (1,5). (a) Enlarge it by scale factor 2, centre the origin, and give all image coordinates. [2] (b) Reflect the original triangle in the line y = x and give its image coordinates. [2] (c) Explain which of these two images is congruent to the original. [1]

questions.label: Question 8 — Grouped mass data
questions.prompt: Forty parcels have masses m kg grouped as follows: 0 < m ≤ 2: 8; 2 < m ≤ 4: 15; 4 < m ≤ 6: 11; 6 < m ≤ 8: 6. (a) State the modal class. [1] (b) Estimate the mean mass. [3] (c) Explain why this mean is an estimate. [1]

questions.label: Question 9 — Algebraic proof
questions.prompt: Prove that the sum of three consecutive integers is divisible by 3. Then show that the sum of their squares is 2 more than a multiple of 3. [4]

questions.label: Question 10 — Inverse proportion
questions.prompt: The time T hours to complete a fixed task is inversely proportional to the number n of identical machines. With 6 machines, T = 15. (a) Find T in terms of n. [2] (b) Find the least whole number of machines needed to finish in at most 8 hours. [2]

questions.label: Question 11 — Functions
questions.prompt: f(x) = 2x + 1 and g(x) = (x − 3)². (a) Find fg(x). [1] (b) Find f⁻¹(x). [2] (c) Solve gf(x) = 0. [1]

questions.label: Question 12 — Inequality region
questions.prompt: On coordinate axes, show the region satisfying x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0, x + y ≤ 6 and y ≤ 2x. State the coordinates of its vertices. [4]

questions.label: Question 13 — Arithmetic series
questions.prompt: An arithmetic sequence has fourth term 17 and tenth term 41. (a) Find its first term and common difference. [2] (b) Find the sum of its first 25 terms. [2]

questions.label: Question 14 — Stationary points
questions.prompt: For y = x³ − 3x² − 9x + 4, find the stationary points and classify each using the signs of the gradient on either side. [5]

questions.label: Question 15 — Kinematics
questions.prompt: A particle's displacement from O is s = t³ − 6t² + 12t metres, where t is time in seconds and 0 ≤ t ≤ 5. (a) Find its velocity and acceleration as functions of t. [2] (b) Find the time at which it is instantaneously at rest. [1] (c) Does it reverse direction at that time? Explain. [2]

questions.label: Question 16 — Nonlinear simultaneous equations
questions.prompt: Solve x² + y² = 25 and y = x + 1, giving both pairs of coordinates. [5]

questions.label: Question 17 — Cone and sphere
questions.prompt: A solid metal cone of radius 6 cm and height 12 cm is melted without loss and cast into spheres of radius 2 cm. (a) Find the cone volume in terms of π. [2] (b) Find the volume of one sphere in terms of π. [1] (c) Find the number of complete spheres and the unused volume. [2]

questions.label: Question 18 — Intersecting chords
questions.prompt: Chords AB and CD intersect inside a circle at P. AP = 3 cm, PB = 8 cm and CP = 4 cm. (a) Find PD. [2] (b) A different circle has centre O and a chord EF of length 16 cm. The perpendicular distance from O to EF is 6 cm. Find the radius, explaining the circle property used. [3]

questions.label: Question 19 — Vector proof
questions.prompt: In triangle OAB, OA = a and OB = b. P divides OA in the ratio OP:PA = 2:1 and Q divides OB in the ratio OQ:QB = 2:1. (a) Express PQ in terms of a and b. [2] (b) Prove that PQ is parallel to AB and state PQ:AB. [2] (c) Find the position vector of the midpoint of PQ. [1]

questions.label: Question 20 — Quartiles
questions.prompt: The ordered data are 2, 4, 6, 7, 9, 11, 14, 16, 18. Exclude the overall median when taking the medians of the two halves. Find the lower quartile, upper quartile and interquartile range. [3]

questions.label: Question 21 — Cumulative frequency
questions.prompt: For 60 times, cumulative frequencies at 0, 10, 20, 30, 40 minutes are 0, 8, 26, 50, 60. (a) Draw a cumulative-frequency graph. [2] (b) Estimate the median using straight-line interpolation between successive points. [1]

questions.label: Question 22 — Comparing distributions
questions.prompt: Group A has minimum 12, lower quartile 18, median 25, upper quartile 31 and maximum 42. Group B has minimum 9, lower quartile 20, median 23, upper quartile 27 and maximum 48. (a) Calculate both interquartile ranges. [2] (b) Compare the typical values and the spread of the middle halves. [2]
